Two organizations advocate for Line 5 Tunnel

Leaders from the Institute for Energy Research (IER) and the Mackinac Center for Public Policy are urging the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers to prioritize and expedite the Environmental Impact Statement (EIS) process for the proposed Enbridge Line 5 Tunnel project. They sent a letter to U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, highlighting the urgent need for the tunnel to protect the Great Lakes and ensure continued energy flow, aligning with President Trump's declaration of a national energy emergency. The organizations emphasize that the tunnel project balances environmental protection with critical energy needs for Midwest families and businesses, and that delays contradict stated environmental goals.

Tell NC regulators to protect local waterways from Enbridge’s T15 Pipeline

Appalachian Voices is urging North Carolina residents to contact the DEQ regarding Enbridge’s proposed 45-mile T15 natural gas pipeline. The pipeline, planned through Rockingham, Caswell, and Person counties, poses risks of water pollution, threatens drinking water supplies, and could contribute to the climate crisis. The organization is asking for more public meetings and stronger environmental protections for the project.

Enbridge completes acquisition PSNC

Enbridge Inc. has completed its acquisition of Public Service Company of North Carolina (PSNC) from Dominion Energy, Inc. PSNC will now operate as Enbridge Gas North Carolina, joining Enbridge's Gas Distribution and Storage Business Unit. This acquisition marks the successful completion of a strategic move to acquire three US-based gas utilities, enhancing Enbridge's low-risk utility business model and expanding its reach in a growing economic region.

Enbridge Finishes Dominion Acquisitions with PSNC Transaction Close

Enbridge Inc. has completed its acquisition of Public Service Company of North Carolina (PSNC) from Dominion Energy, Inc., marking the finalization of its strategic acquisition of three gas utilities announced in September 2023. PSNC will operate as Enbridge Gas North Carolina, expanding Enbridge's presence in the U.S. utility sector across Ohio, North Carolina, Utah, Idaho, and Wyoming. The total acquisition of the three utilities amounted to $14 billion (CAD 19 billion), strengthening Enbridge's low-risk utility business model and emphasizing the need for natural gas infrastructure.

Enbridge Inc. to Host Webcast to Discuss 2025 Third Quarter Results on November 7

Enbridge Inc. announced it will host a conference call and webcast on November 7, 2025, at 7 a.m. MT (9 a.m. ET) to discuss its 2025 third-quarter financial results and provide a business update. The event will include remarks from the executive team followed by a Q&A session for analysts and investors. Enbridge will release its financial results before market open on the same day.

New generation of tunneling is safe, proven

Enbridge's Great Lakes Tunnel Project aims to build a new segment of the Line 5 pipeline under the Straits of Mackinac using advanced tunneling technology. The article highlights the safety and proven nature of modern tunnel boring machines (TBMs), citing numerous successful projects globally and detailing how this technology will improve energy delivery and potentially other utilities in Michigan. Enbridge is awaiting a federal permit to begin construction, emphasizing the project's importance for Michigan residents and the region.

Great Lakes Tunnel Project: EGLE public comment period

The Michigan Department of Environment, Great Lakes, and Energy (EGLE) is currently accepting public comments on Enbridge's permit applications for surface facilities related to the Great Lakes Tunnel and its construction. The public comment period runs through August 29, 2025, with a virtual public hearing scheduled for August 19, 2025, at 6 p.m. ET. Enbridge encourages interested parties to share their opinions during this period.

Enbridge Mulls Expanding Pipeline Capacity to U.S. Gulf Coast Due to Soaring Oil Demand

Canadian pipeline operator Enbridge Inc. is considering expanding its North American Mainline network following strong demand for additional oil transport capacity to the U.S. Gulf Coast. An "open season" for its Flanagan South pipeline was oversubscribed, indicating robust interest from shippers. Enbridge plans to make a final investment decision this year on the first phase of expansion, aiming to add 150,000 barrels of capacity due to increasing Canadian oil sands production and U.S. demand.

Power under pressure: Meeting demand in an uncertain world

This article discusses the growing challenges in meeting energy demand due to political and economic uncertainty, extreme weather, and surging power requirements. Enbridge advocates for a diversified "all-of-the-above" energy strategy, emphasizing the critical role of natural gas alongside renewables to ensure grid stability and power essential industries. The company highlights its extensive energy infrastructure and experience in maintaining reliable energy flow in an increasingly complex environment.

Enbridge Eyes New Pipeline to Boost Canadian Oil Flows in US

Enbridge Inc. and Energy Transfer LP are exploring a new pipeline project, the Southern Illinois Connector, to increase crude oil transportation capacity from Flanagan, Illinois, to the US Gulf Coast. This initiative aims to move up to 200,000 barrels of Canadian oil sands production daily by upgrading existing systems and adding a new segment. The project is a direct response to industry demand for enhanced oil shipping capacity to US markets.
